provider: Sia host (hostd) - supply side / the arbitrage test

free_tier.stated: you set your own price; network median is $1.17/TB/month storage and $2.25/TB download (siascan), $1.30 KS/TB/month

egress.terms: you are PAID for egress ($2.25/TB median) rather than charged

interface_detail: hostd daemon (Docker/Linux/macOS/Windows), open ports, Siacoin wallet
tooling: hostd desktop app v0.46.1, hostd CLI, siascan for competitor pricing
chaining: earn SC, buy storage with SC on the same network - the only place where the earn and spend currencies actually match
limits_note: THE ARBITRAGE DOES NOT EXIST, and Sia's own numbers show it precisely. A host earns the median $1.17/TB/mo; a renter pays $2-3/TB/mo for the same terabyte (the $3 figure includes 3x redundancy). So contributing N TB of disk buys you N x 1.17/3 = 0.39N TB of retail storage - you must contribute ~2.6x the disk you want to consume, and you must also lock collateral at '2-3x your base storage price' in SC, keep the machine online, and forward ports. Storing 20 TiB on Sia costs $60-70/mo, which means hosting ~51-60 TB of other people's data to break even.
reliability_note: Lose the data or fail a proof and the collateral is burned; a single drive failure is a total loss for that contract.
